steps.headline: Is a separate acceptance deck at the end one deck too many?

options.label: Keep the acceptance deck (recommended)
options.summary: You tick the human rows after the work exists, and see every machine verdict beside them. One extra deck per feature.

options.label: Fold the human rows into the contract
options.summary: One fewer deck, but you would tick 'this holds' rows before anything is built — a promise, not a check.

steps.headline: When the build contradicts an approved design and you do not answer, proceed on a marked default or always stop?

options.label: Proceed on a marked default (recommended)
options.summary: The reopen deck names a default; if it times out the build continues and the acceptance deck carries a 'decided without you' row you can veto. This is what makes a one-shot build possible.

options.label: Always stop and wait
options.summary: Nothing is ever decided for you, but every contradiction is a hard stop until you return.

steps.headline: Build tasks carry a description by default, with pre-written code only for cross-repo, stored-data or strict-order work?

options.label: Description by default (recommended)
options.summary: The technical design and its review round happen on every feature either way. Subagents write the code from a task description plus the contract; pre-written code only where getting it wrong up front is costly.

options.label: Always pre-write the code
options.summary: Every task ships with its code typed out, as the 1,770-line plan for this feature did. Half of that was corrected after review and its line numbers were stale on day one.

steps.headline: Commit the deck answers files to git?

options.label: Commit them (recommended)
options.summary: They hold your words verbatim and are the only record of decisions; ignored for three months, they lived on one disk. Already done on this branch — 27 files.

options.label: Copy them beside each contract at sign-off instead
options.summary: Keeps a feature folder self-contained, but the rounds' history stays untracked and a clean checkout has none of it.
